content.value_statement: Animated floating components can lose keyboard focus when CSS starts at opacity zero. This skill explains a retry pattern and tests for Select, DropdownMenu, and Popover components.
actual_capabilities: Explains why CSS fade animations can block immediate focus calls.
Shows a retry-based focus strategy using animation frame timing and short delays.
Documents affected Select, DropdownMenu, and Popover focus flows.
Lists keyboard symptoms for animated floating content failures.
Describes Playwright test coverage for animated keyboard interactions.
limitations: It is guidance documentation, not an automated code transformation tool.
It focuses on opacity-based animation timing, not every browser focus edge case.
Examples are tailored to Summit UI naming and component structure.
It does not verify behavior in a live application by itself.

use_cases.title: Repair animated dropdown keyboard behavior
use_cases.description: Diagnose why arrow keys stop working after a dropdown opens with CSS animation.

use_cases.title: Document accessible focus timing decisions
use_cases.description: Capture the reason for retrying focus after animated floating content renders.

use_cases.title: Plan regression tests for animated components
use_cases.description: Define keyboard tests that confirm Enter, arrow keys, selection, and Escape still work.

prompt_templates.title: Identify the focus symptom
prompt_templates.prompt: Use animated-focus to explain why my animated dropdown opens but arrow keys still act on the trigger button.

prompt_templates.title: Apply the retry pattern
prompt_templates.prompt: Use animated-focus to adapt my floating component focus helper for CSS animations that begin at opacity zero.

prompt_templates.title: Review component coverage
prompt_templates.prompt: Use animated-focus to review Select, DropdownMenu, and Popover focus flows for animation timing gaps.

prompt_templates.title: Design regression tests
prompt_templates.prompt: Use animated-focus to create a Playwright test plan for keyboard navigation across animated floating components.

output_examples.input: Explain why keyboard navigation fails only when fade animation classes are enabled.
output_examples.output: The element is rendered but begins invisible, so the browser can reject the first focus request. Focus stays on the trigger.

output_examples.input: Suggest tests for animated Select and DropdownMenu components.
output: Open each component with Enter while animation classes are active.
Verify arrow keys move through items after the open animation starts.
Confirm Enter selects or activates the focused item.
Confirm Escape closes the floating content.

output_examples.output: Attempt focus after one animation frame, verify the active element, then retry briefly while the animation becomes focusable.

best_practices: Verify focus success by checking the active element after each attempt.
Keep retry windows short so keyboard users do not feel input lag.
Test animated and non-animated component states with the same keyboard flows.
anti_patterns: Do not assume focus succeeds immediately after rendering animated content.
Do not fix focus timing by adding a long unconditional delay.
Do not test only mouse interactions for animated floating components.

faq.question: What problem does this skill address?
faq.answer: It addresses keyboard focus failures caused by floating content that starts invisible during CSS animation.

faq.question: Which components are covered?
faq.answer: The guidance names Select, DropdownMenu, and Popover components with animated floating content.

faq.question: Does the skill execute commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It is a Markdown guidance document and only includes examples for developers to review.

faq.question: Why use retry logic instead of one delay?
faq.answer: Retry logic keeps the wait short while allowing the browser to accept focus after animation begins.

faq.question: How should teams validate the fix?
faq.answer: Teams should test Enter, arrow keys, selection or activation, and Escape with animation classes enabled.

faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
